target_customer: Small merchants and creators in Latin America who sell through social media
problem: Merchants in developing markets sell over social media and chat but lack an easy storefront, payments and fulfillment in one place.
business_model: Platform fees on payments and subscriptions for storefront tools
product_category: Social commerce operating system for merchants

founders.name: Felipe Echandi
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page; no background listed.

founders.name: Jose Varela
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page; two time founder and CTO with background in B2B wholesale logistics and B2C ecommerce and payment processing.

technical_complexity.rationale: Storefront, payments and fulfillment integration across several Latin American countries is standard commerce engineering with payments partners.

defensibility.rationale: Storefront tools are easy to copy, with local payment integrations the only stated advantage.

market_need_then: Merchants in Latin America were selling through social media; the company reported around 400 small businesses using the app according to a Panamerican World snippet, unread in full.

branding.name_origin: Spanish cuanto means how much, which fits a pricing and payments product, but no source states this as the origin.
branding.domain_note: Uses cuanto.app and web.cuanto.app; many unrelated products share the name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish first with a note that the company is backed by Y Combinator

brand_strength.rationale: A short Spanish word that fits the product, but shared with several unrelated apps and with no brand coverage found.

pivots.from: Helping Latin American merchants launch online and sell over social media
pivots.to: Operating system for developing world merchants covering storefront, payments and fulfillment
pivots.why: Broadened scope per the YC page; not described as a pivot

outcome_analysis: Cuanto is a four person Panama company that says it was the first Panamanian startup in YC, joining Winter 2019 to help Latin American merchants sell through social media. It remains active but no verified funding, traction or later milestones were found, so the outcome is unknown rather than a failure.
notes: Unverified funding: Persana lists about 1.4M dollars of pre-seed in April 2019, and a Panamerican World snippet mentions a 150K dollar investment; both single sources, not recorded. No competitor source dated near 2019 was found. The founding year is 2017 per one source and 2018 per YC. The Panamerican World article fetch returned empty.
